findings.label: Suppliers with Current Red Flags
findings.detail: 6 current suppliers have Companies House compliance issues (historical payments were made before breaches started)

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 369 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 2297 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: Balance Sheet Cost Centres (P) spent 2.0x their monthly average in March (£1.7M above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Signal Traffic Management Ltd (2.7 day avg, 1651 payments, £2.9M)

findings.label: Benford's Law Analysis
findings.detail: Digit distribution across 358,110 transactions shows χ²=13328.47 (statistically significant due to large sample size), but max digit deviation is only 4.1% — within the normal range for UK council spending patterns. No practical evidence of fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 358,110+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (4.1%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 358,110 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 2.72% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=358,110.

findings.label: Weak Competition Indicators
findings.detail: 3 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: CADAVER TRANSPORTATION AND STORAGE ON BEHALF OF HM (£512.0K)
findings.context_note: Contracts Finder does not publish bid counts. These flags use proxy signals: tender periods under 14 days and awards within 7 days of deadline. Short timelines may have legitimate explanations (framework call-offs, urgency).

findings.label: High-Risk Councillors
findings.detail: 28 councillors scored 'high risk' in integrity assessment across 36 data sources. Most common flags: undeclared interests, supplier conflicts, and company compliance issues.

key_findings.title: 10 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Signal Traffic Management Ltd — every 2.7 days (1651 payments, £2.9M)

key_findings.title: PREMIER TAXIS LEICESTER LTD: 9218 transactions totalling £15.3M
key_findings.description: Averaging £1.7K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier

key_findings.title: AI DOGE covers 42% of £893.7M GOV.UK outturn
key_findings.description: Spending >£500 threshold means smaller transactions are excluded. Largest gaps: Education services, Highways and transport services, Children Social Care. This is expected — not a data quality issue.
